sanskrit: tataḥ sukanyā saṃvītā tāv uvāca surottamau śaryātitanayāṃ vittaṃ bhāryāṃ ca cyavanasya mām
english: Then Sukanyā, modestly dressed, addressed those two foremost of gods: "Know me to be the daughter of Śaryāti and the wife of Cyavana."

sanskrit: athāśvinau prahasyaitām abrūtāṃ punar eva tu kathaṃ tvam asi kalyāṇi pitrā dattā gatādhvane
english: The two Aśvins then laughed and spoke to her again: "How is it, fair one, that your father gave you in marriage to one who had already passed his prime?"

sanskrit: bhrājase vanamadhye tvaṃ vidyut saudāminī yathā na deveṣv api tulyāṃ hi tvayā paśyāva bhāmini
english: "You shine in the midst of this forest like a flash of lightning in the clouds. We see none equal to you even among the celestials, O passionate one."

sanskrit: sarvābharaṇasaṃpannā paramāmbaradhāriṇī śobhethās tv anavadyāṅgi na tv evaṃ malapaṅkinī
english: "Adorned with all ornaments and clad in the finest garments, you would shine splendidly, O blameless-limbed one — not thus smeared with mud and filth."

sanskrit: kasmād evaṃvidhā bhūtvā jarājarjaritaṃ patim tvam upāsse ha kalyāṇi kāmabhogabahiṣkṛtam
english: "Why, being what you are, do you attend upon a husband shriveled by old age, O fair one — one excluded from the pleasures of love?"

sanskrit: asamarthaṃ paritrāṇe poṣaṇe ca śucismite sādhu cyavanam utsṛjya varayasvaikam āvayoḥ patyarthaṃ devagarbhābhe mā vṛthā yauvanaṃ kṛthāḥ
english: "One incapable of protection or sustenance, O bright-smiling one — it would be well to abandon Cyavana and choose one of us as a husband, O you who are like the offspring of gods. Do not let your youth go to waste."

sanskrit: evam uktā sukanyā tu surau tāv idam abravīt ratāhaṃ cyavane patyau maivaṃ mā paryaśaṅkithāḥ
english: Thus addressed, Sukanyā said to those two gods: "I am devoted to Cyavana as my husband — do not think otherwise of me."

sanskrit: tāv abrūtāṃ punas tv enām āvāṃ devabhiṣagvarau yuvānaṃ rūpasaṃpannaṃ kariṣyāvaḥ patiṃ tava
english: The two then spoke to her again: "We are the foremost physicians of the gods. We shall make your husband young and handsome."

sanskrit: tatas tasyāvayoś caiva patim ekatamaṃ vṛṇu etena samayenainam āmantraya varānane
english: "Then choose one among us three — your husband included — and convey this offer to him, O fair-faced one."

sanskrit: sā tayor vacanād rājann upasaṃgamya bhārgavam uvāca vākyaṃ yat tābhyām uktaṃ bhṛgusutaṃ prati
english: At their word, O king, she approached the son of Bhṛgu and reported to that descendant of Bhṛgu what the two had said.

sanskrit: tac chrutvā cyavano bhāryām uvāca kriyatām iti bhartrā sā samanujñātā kriyatām ity athābravīt
english: Hearing that, Cyavana said to his wife: "Let it be done." Permitted by her husband, she then said: "Let it be done."

sanskrit: śrutvā tad aśvinau vākyaṃ tat tasyāḥ kriyatām iti ūcatū rājaputrīṃ tāṃ patis tava viśatv apaḥ
english: The Aśvins, hearing her words of consent, said to that princess: "Let your husband enter the waters."

sanskrit: tato 'mbhaś cyavanaḥ śīghraṃ rūpārthī praviveśa ha aśvināv api tad rājan saraḥ praviśatāṃ prabho
english: Then Cyavana quickly entered the waters, seeking a new form. The two Aśvins also, O king, entered that lake, O lord.

sanskrit: tato muhūrtād uttīrṇāḥ sarve te sarasas tataḥ divyarūpadharāḥ sarve yuvāno mṛṣṭakuṇḍalāḥ tulyarūpadharāś caiva manasaḥ prītivardhanāḥ
english: After a moment, all three emerged from that lake bearing divine forms — all young, wearing polished earrings, all alike in appearance, gladdening the heart.

sanskrit: te 'bruvan sahitāḥ sarve vṛṇīṣvānyatamaṃ śubhe asmākam īpsitaṃ bhadre patitve varavarṇini yatra vāpy abhikāmāsi taṃ vṛṇīṣva suśobhane
english: All three together said: "Choose one of us, O beautiful one, as the husband you desire, O auspicious and fair-complexioned one. Whomever your heart inclines to, him choose, O most lovely one."

sanskrit: sā samīkṣya tu tān sarvāṃs tulyarūpadharān sthitān niścitya manasā buddhyā devī vavre svakaṃ patim
english: She observed all three standing there with identical forms, and the blessed one, resolving in her mind and understanding, chose her own husband.

sanskrit: labdhvā tu cyavano bhāryāṃ vayorūpaṃ ca vāñchitam hṛṣṭo 'bravīn mahātejās tau nāsatyāv idaṃ vacaḥ
english: Cyavana, having regained his wife and the youth and form he had desired, was delighted, and that great-spirited one spoke these words to the two Nāsatyas:

sanskrit: yathāhaṃ rūpasaṃpanno vayasā ca samanvitaḥ kṛto bhavadbhyāṃ vṛddhaḥ san bhāryāṃ ca prāptavān imām
english: "As I, though old, have been made by you endowed with beauty and youth, and have regained this my wife —"

sanskrit: tasmād yuvāṃ kariṣyāmi prītyāhaṃ somapīthinau miṣato devarājasya satyam etad bravīmi vām
english: "— therefore, with affection, I shall make you both drinkers of soma, even before the eyes of the king of gods. This I declare to you in truth."

sanskrit: tac chrutvā hṛṣṭamanasau divaṃ tau pratijagmatuḥ cyavano 'pi sukanyā ca surāv iva vijahratuḥ
english: Hearing that, those two, with gladdened hearts, departed to heaven. Cyavana and Sukanyā also sported together like two celestials.

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca tataḥ śrutvā tu śaryātir vayaḥsthaṃ cyavanaṃ kṛtam saṃhṛṣṭaḥ senayā sārdham upāyād bhārgavāśramam
english: Lomaśa said: Then, having heard that Cyavana had been restored to his prime, Śaryāti was overjoyed and came with his army to the hermitage of Bhṛgu's descendant.

sanskrit: cyavanaṃ ca sukanyāṃ ca dṛṣṭvā devasutāv iva reme mahīpaḥ śaryātiḥ kṛtsnāṃ prāpya mahīm iva
english: Seeing Cyavana and Sukanyā, who looked like two children of the gods, king Śaryāti rejoiced as if he had gained the entire earth.

sanskrit: ṛṣiṇā satkṛtas tena sabhāryaḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ upopaviṣṭaḥ kalyāṇīḥ kathāś cakre mahāmanāḥ
english: Honored by that seer, the lord of the earth sat down with his wife and the great-minded one engaged in auspicious conversation.

sanskrit: athainaṃ bhārgavo rājann uvāca parisāntvayan yājayiṣyāmi rājaṃs tvāṃ saṃbhārān upakalpaya
english: Then the descendant of Bhṛgu, consoling him, O king, said: "I shall perform a sacrifice for you, O king — make ready the materials."

sanskrit: tataḥ paramasaṃhṛṣṭaḥ śaryātiḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ cyavanasya mahārāja tad vākyaṃ pratyapūjayat
english: Then Śaryāti, lord of the earth, most greatly delighted, O great king, honored that word of Cyavana.

sanskrit: praśaste 'hani yajñīye sarvakāmasamṛddhimat kārayām āsa śaryātir yajñāyatanam uttamam
english: On an auspicious day fit for sacrifice, Śaryāti had an excellent sacrificial hall constructed, filled with every desired abundance.

sanskrit: tatrainaṃ cyavano rājan yājayām āsa bhārgavaḥ adbhutāni ca tatrāsan yāni tāni nibodha me
english: There the descendant of Bhṛgu, Cyavana, officiated at the sacrifice for that king. And there were wonders there — hear them from me.

sanskrit: agṛhṇāc cyavanaḥ somam aśvinor devayos tadā tam indro vārayām āsa gṛhyamāṇaṃ tayor graham
english: Cyavana then took the soma portion for the two divine Aśvins, but Indra tried to stop that cup being taken for them.

sanskrit: indra uvāca ubhāv etau na somārhau nāsatyāv iti me matiḥ bhiṣajau devaputrāṇāṃ karmaṇā naivam arhataḥ
english: Indra said: "Both these Nāsatyas are not worthy of soma — such is my opinion. Being physicians to the sons of gods by their function, they are not entitled to it."

sanskrit: cyavana uvāca māvamaṃsthā mahātmānau rūpadraviṇavattarau yau cakratur māṃ maghavan vṛndārakam ivājaram
english: Cyavana said: "Do not despise those two great souls, superior in beauty and worth, O Maghavan, who made me ageless as if among the immortals."

sanskrit: ṛte tvāṃ vibudhāṃś cānyān kathaṃ vai nārhataḥ savam aśvināv api devendra devau viddhi puraṃdara
english: "Apart from you and the other gods — how could they not deserve the soma feast? Know the Aśvins too as gods, O Indra, O destroyer of citadels."

sanskrit: indra uvāca cikitsakau karmakarau kāmarūpasamanvitau loke carantau martyānāṃ kathaṃ somam ihārhataḥ
english: Indra said: "They are healers, doers of tasks, who assume forms at will and roam the mortal world — how can they be worthy of soma here?"

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca etad eva yadā vākyam āmreḍayati vāsavaḥ anādṛtya tataḥ śakraṃ grahaṃ jagrāha bhārgavaḥ
english: Lomaśa said: When Vāsava kept repeating this same argument, the descendant of Bhṛgu, disregarding Śakra, took the cup.

sanskrit: grahīṣyantaṃ tu taṃ somam aśvinor uttamaṃ tadā samīkṣya balabhid deva idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Then the god who had slain Bala, seeing him about to take that excellent soma for the Aśvins, spoke these words:

sanskrit: ābhyām arthāya somaṃ tvaṃ grahīṣyasi yadi svayam vajraṃ te prahariṣyāmi ghorarūpam anuttamam
english: "If you yourself take the soma for those two, I will hurl at you my thunderbolt, fearsome and unequalled in form."

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ smayann indram abhivīkṣya sa bhārgavaḥ jagrāha vidhivat somam aśvibhyām uttamaṃ graham
english: Thus addressed, the descendant of Bhṛgu, smiling, looked at Indra and took, according to the proper rite, the excellent soma cup for the Aśvins.

sanskrit: tato 'smai prāharad vajraṃ ghorarūpaṃ śacīpatiḥ tasya praharato bāhuṃ stambhayām āsa bhārgavaḥ
english: Then the lord of Śacī hurled his fearsome thunderbolt at him, but the descendant of Bhṛgu paralyzed his arm as it was about to strike.

sanskrit: saṃstambhayitvā cyavano juhuve mantrato 'nalam kṛtyārthī sumahātejā devaṃ hiṃsitum udyataḥ
english: Having paralyzed him, Cyavana, of surpassing splendor, poured oblations into the fire with mantras, intent on performing a rite and ready to harm the god.

sanskrit: tataḥ kṛtyā samabhavad ṛṣes tasya tapobalāt mado nāma mahāvīryo bṛhatkāyo mahāsuraḥ śarīraṃ yasya nirdeṣṭum aśakyaṃ tu surāsuraiḥ
english: Then from the power of that seer's austerities there arose from the rite a mighty being named Mada — a great asura of immense valor and vast body, whose form could not be described by gods or demons alike.

sanskrit: tasyāsyam abhavad ghoraṃ tīkṣṇāgradaśanaṃ mahat hanur ekā sthitā tasya bhūmāv ekā divaṃ gatā
english: His mouth was terrifying and immense, with sharp-tipped teeth; one of his jaws rested on the earth and the other reached up to the sky.

sanskrit: catasra āyatā daṃṣṭrā yojanānāṃ śataṃ śatam itare tv asya daśanā babhūvur daśayojanāḥ prākārasadṛśākārāḥ śūlāgrasamadarśanāḥ
english: His four long fangs each measured a hundred times a hundred leagues, while his other teeth were ten leagues each, shaped like ramparts and appearing like the tips of spears.

sanskrit: bāhū parvatasaṃkāśāv āyatāv ayutaṃ samau netre raviśaśiprakhye vaktram antakasaṃnibham
english: His two arms, like mountains, stretched ten thousand leagues each; his eyes resembled the sun and moon; his face was like that of Death himself.

sanskrit: lelihañ jihvayā vaktraṃ vidyuccapalalolayā vyāttānano ghoradṛṣṭir grasann iva jagad balāt
english: He licked his mouth with a tongue flickering like lightning, his jaws gaping wide, his glance terrible, as if swallowing the entire world by force.

sanskrit: sa bhakṣayiṣyan saṃkruddhaḥ śatakratum upādravat mahatā ghorarūpeṇa lokāñ śabdena nādayan
english: Enraged and about to devour him, he charged at the performer of a hundred sacrifices with his mighty and fearsome form, making all the worlds resound with his roar.

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca taṃ dṛṣṭvā ghoravadanaṃ madaṃ devaḥ śatakratuḥ āyāntaṃ bhakṣayiṣyantaṃ vyāttānanam ivāntakam
english: Lomaśa said: Seeing Mada of the dreadful mouth, coming to devour him with jaws agape like Death himself, the god of a hundred sacrifices —

sanskrit: bhayāt saṃstambhitabhujaḥ sṛkkiṇī lelihan muhuḥ tato 'bravīd devarājaś cyavanaṃ bhayapīḍitaḥ
english: — his arm already paralyzed with fear, repeatedly licking the corners of his mouth, the king of the gods then spoke to Cyavana, oppressed by fear:

sanskrit: somārhāv aśvināv etāv adya prabhṛti bhārgava bhaviṣyataḥ satyam etad vaco brahman bravīmi te
english: "The Aśvins shall be worthy of soma from this day forward, O descendant of Bhṛgu. This word I speak to you truly, O brahmin."

sanskrit: na te mithyā samārambho bhavatv eṣa paro vidhiḥ jānāmi cāhaṃ viprarṣe na mithyā tvaṃ kariṣyasi
english: "Let your undertaking not be in vain — this shall be the highest rule henceforth. I know, O seer among brahmins, that you will not act falsely."

sanskrit: somārhāv aśvināv etau yathaivādya kṛtau tvayā bhūya eva tu te vīryaṃ prakāśed iti bhārgava
english: "Just as the Aśvins have this day been made worthy of soma by you, O descendant of Bhṛgu, may your power shine even more brightly."

sanskrit: sukanyāyāḥ pituś cāsya loke kīrtiḥ prathed iti ato mayaitad vihitaṃ tava vīryaprakāśanam tasmāt prasādaṃ kuru me bhavatv etad yathecchasi
english: "And may the fame of Sukanyā's father spread through the world — it is for this that I arranged this manifestation of your power. Therefore be gracious to me; let this be as you wish."

sanskrit: evam uktasya śakreṇa cyavanasya mahātmanaḥ sa manyur vyagamac chīghraṃ mumoca ca puraṃdaram
english: When Śakra had spoken thus to the great-souled Cyavana, his anger quickly departed and he released the destroyer of citadels.

sanskrit: madaṃ ca vyabhajad rājan pāne strīṣu ca vīryavān akṣeṣu mṛgayāyāṃ ca pūrvasṛṣṭaṃ punaḥ punaḥ
english: And the mighty one divided Mada, O king, distributing him repeatedly — as previously created — among wine, women, dice, and the hunt.

sanskrit: tathā madaṃ viniṣkṣipya śakraṃ saṃtarpya cendunā aśvibhyāṃ sahitān devān yājayitvā ca taṃ nṛpam
english: Having thus dispersed Mada, and having satisfied Śakra with the soma, and having officiated at that king's sacrifice with the Aśvins included among the gods —

sanskrit: vikhyāpya vīryaṃ sarveṣu lokeṣu vadatāṃ varaḥ sukanyayā sahāraṇye vijahārānuraktayā
english: — having made his power known throughout all the worlds, that best of speakers then sported in the forest with the devoted Sukanyā.

sanskrit: tasyaitad dvijasaṃghuṣṭaṃ saro rājan prakāśate atra tvaṃ saha sodaryaiḥ pitṝn devāṃś ca tarpaya
english: This lake of his, O king, resounds with the chanting of twice-born men and shines with glory. Here you should satisfy the ancestors and the gods together with your brothers.

sanskrit: etad dṛṣṭvā mahīpāla sikatākṣaṃ ca bhārata saindhavāraṇyam āsādya kulyānāṃ kuru darśanam puṣkareṣu mahārāja sarveṣu ca jalaṃ spṛśa
english: Having seen this, O lord of the earth, O Bhārata, and reaching the Saindhava forest with its sandy shallows, behold the streams. O great king, touch the water at all the lotus pools.

sanskrit: ārcīkaparvataś caiva nivāso vai manīṣiṇām sadāphalaḥ sadāsroto marutāṃ sthānam uttamam caityāś caite bahuśatās tridaśānāṃ yudhiṣṭhira
english: The Ārcīka mountain is indeed the abode of the wise, ever fruitful, ever flowing, the supreme station of the Maruts. These hundreds of sacred shrines here belong to the thirty gods, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: etac candramasas tīrtham ṛṣayaḥ paryupāsate vaikhānasāś ca ṛṣayo vālakhilyās tathaiva ca
english: This is the sacred ford of the Moon, worshipped by seers — the Vaikhānasa sages and likewise the Vālakhilyas attend upon it.

sanskrit: śṛṅgāṇi trīṇi puṇyāṇi trīṇi prasravaṇāni ca sarvāṇy anuparikramya yathākāmam upaspṛśa
english: The three sacred peaks and the three springs — circumambulate all of them and touch the waters as you wish.

sanskrit: śaṃtanuś cātra kaunteya śunakaś ca narādhipa naranārāyaṇau cobhau sthānaṃ prāptāḥ sanātanam
english: Here, O son of Kuntī, O lord of men, Śaṃtanu, Śunaka, and both Nara and Nārāyaṇa have attained the eternal abode.

sanskrit: iha nityaśayā devāḥ pitaraś ca maharṣibhiḥ ārcīkaparvate tepus tān yajasva yudhiṣṭhira
english: Here the gods who dwell eternally, and the ancestors, practised austerities on the Ārcīka mountain along with the great seers — worship them here, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: iha te vai carūn prāśnann ṛṣayaś ca viśāṃ pate yamunā cākṣayasrotāḥ kṛṣṇaś ceha taporataḥ
english: Here the sages partook of the ritual rice-cakes, O lord of peoples. The Yamunā with its inexhaustible stream is here, and Kṛṣṇa is engaged in austerities in this place.

sanskrit: yamau ca bhīmasenaś ca kṛṣṇā cāmitrakarśana sarve cātra gamiṣyāmaḥ sukṛśāḥ sutapasvinaḥ
english: The twins, Bhīmasena, Kṛṣṇā — all of us will go there, O crusher of enemies, lean and deeply practised in austerities.

sanskrit: etat prasravaṇaṃ puṇyam indrasya manujādhipa yatra dhātā vidhātā ca varuṇaś cordhvam āgatāḥ
english: This is the sacred spring of Indra, O lord of men, where Dhātṛ, Vidhātṛ, and Varuṇa came in ancient times.

sanskrit: iha te nyavasan rājan kṣāntāḥ paramadharmiṇaḥ maitrāṇām ṛjubuddhīnām ayaṃ girivaraḥ śubhaḥ
english: Here they dwelt, O king — forbearing and supremely righteous; this finest of mountains is auspicious for those of friendly and upright mind.

sanskrit: eṣā sā yamunā rājan rājarṣigaṇasevitā nānāyajñacitā rājan puṇyā pāpabhayāpahā
english: This is that Yamunā, O king, attended upon by hosts of royal sages, adorned with many sacrifices, O king — holy, dispelling the fear of sin.

sanskrit: atra rājā maheṣvāso māndhātāyajata svayam sahadevaś ca kaunteya somako dadatāṃ varaḥ
english: Here king Māndhātā, the great archer, himself performed sacrifice; and Sahadeva, O son of Kuntī, and Somaka, the foremost of the generous, also did so.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca māndhātā rājaśārdūlas triṣu lokeṣu viśrutaḥ kathaṃ jāto mahābrahman yauvanāśvo nṛpottamaḥ kathaṃ caitāṃ parāṃ kāṣṭhāṃ prāptavān amitadyutiḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: "Māndhātā, that tiger among kings, is renowned throughout the three worlds — how was he born, O great brahmin? That best of kings, the son of Yuvanāśva, of boundless splendor — how did he attain this supreme eminence?"

sanskrit: yasya lokās trayo vaśyā viṣṇor iva mahātmanaḥ etad icchāmy ahaṃ śrotuṃ caritaṃ tasya dhīmataḥ
english: "The three worlds were subject to him like those of the great-souled Viṣṇu — I wish to hear the deeds of that wise one."

sanskrit: yathā māndhātṛśabdaś ca tasya śakrasamadyuteḥ janma cāprativīryasya kuśalo hy asi bhāṣitum
english: "And how did the name Māndhātā come to him who equals Śakra in splendor, and whose valor was unmatched? For you are skilled in narrating."

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca śṛṇuṣvāvahito rājan rājñas tasya mahātmanaḥ yathā māndhātṛśabdo vai lokeṣu parigīyate
english: Lomaśa said: "Listen attentively, O king, to how the name Māndhātā of that great-souled king is sung throughout the worlds."

sanskrit: ikṣvākuvaṃśaprabhavo yuvanāśvo mahīpatiḥ so 'yajat pṛthivīpāla kratubhir bhūridakṣiṇaiḥ
english: "Yuvanāśva, lord of the earth, sprung from the lineage of Ikṣvāku, O guardian of the earth, performed sacrifices with abundant gifts."

sanskrit: aśvamedhasahasraṃ ca prāpya dharmabhṛtāṃ varaḥ anyaiś ca kratubhir mukhyair vividhair āptadakṣiṇaiḥ
english: "Having performed a thousand horse sacrifices, that best of those who uphold dharma, and also other foremost and various sacrifices with ample gifts —"

sanskrit: anapatyas tu rājarṣiḥ sa mahātmā dṛḍhavrataḥ mantriṣv ādhāya tad rājyaṃ vananityo babhūva ha
english: "— yet that great-souled royal seer, firm in his vows, remained without a son; he entrusted the kingdom to his ministers and took to living in the forest."

sanskrit: śāstradṛṣṭena vidhinā saṃyojyātmānam ātmanā pipāsāśuṣkahṛdayaḥ praviveśāśramaṃ bhṛgoḥ
english: "Uniting himself with his own self by the rule prescribed in scripture, his heart parched with thirst, he entered the hermitage of Bhṛgu."

sanskrit: tām eva rātriṃ rājendra mahātmā bhṛgunandanaḥ iṣṭiṃ cakāra saudyumner maharṣiḥ putrakāraṇāt
english: "That very night, O lord of kings, the great-souled son of Bhṛgu, the great seer, performed a rite for the sake of a son for Saudyumni."

sanskrit: saṃbhṛto mantrapūtena vāriṇā kalaśo mahān tatrātiṣṭhata rājendra pūrvam eva samāhitaḥ yat prāśya prasavet tasya patnī śakrasamaṃ sutam
english: "A great jar filled with water consecrated by mantras stood there, O lord of kings, having been prepared beforehand with concentrated intent — by drinking from it, the wife of him would give birth to a son equal to Śakra."

sanskrit: taṃ nyasya vedyāṃ kalaśaṃ suṣupus te maharṣayaḥ rātrijāgaraṇaśrāntāḥ saudyumniḥ samatītya tān
english: "Having placed that jar on the altar, the great seers fell asleep, wearied from their vigil through the night; and Saudyumni, passing them by —"

sanskrit: śuṣkakaṇṭhaḥ pipāsārtaḥ pāṇīyārthī bhṛśaṃ nṛpaḥ taṃ praviśyāśramaṃ śrāntaḥ pāṇīyaṃ so 'bhyayācata
english: "— the king, parched of throat, sorely tormented by thirst, craving water, entered that hermitage exhausted and begged for water."

sanskrit: tasya śrāntasya śuṣkeṇa kaṇṭhena krośatas tadā nāśrauṣīt kaś cana tadā śakuner iva vāśitam
english: "As he, exhausted, cried out with his parched throat, no one then heard him — like the cry of a bird."
